title.zh: 卷二百五十一 列傳第十 韓令坤 慕容延釗 符彥卿
title.en: Volume 251 Biographies 10: Han Lingkun, Murong Yanzhao, Fu Yanqing
title.raw: 卷二百五十一 列傳第十 韓令坤 慕容延釗 符彥卿 Volume 251 Biographies 10: Han Lingkun, Murong Yanzhao, Fu Yanqing

sentences.zh: 韓令坤

translations.literal: Han Lingkun
translations.idiomatic: Han Lingkun

sentences.zh: 韓令坤，磁州武安人。

translations.literal: Han Lingkun was a man of Wu'an in Cizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Han Lingkun was a native of Wu'an in Cizhou.

sentences.zh: 父倫，少以勇敢隸成德軍兵籍，累遷徐州下邳鎮將兼守禦指揮使。

translations.literal: His father Lun, in youth noted for courage, was enrolled on the rolls of the Chengde Army; he was repeatedly promoted to garrison commander of Xiapi in Xuzhou and concurrently director of the frontier defense command.
translations.idiomatic: His father Lun had been known since youth for his bravery and served on the rolls of the Chengde Army, rising through repeated promotions to become commander of the Xiapi garrison in Xuzhou and concurrently head of the frontier defense command.

sentences.zh: 世宗以令坤貴，擢陳州行軍司馬，及令坤領陳州，徙倫許州。

translations.literal: Because Lingkun had become eminent, the Emperor Shizong promoted Lun to army aide of Chenzhou; when Lingkun took charge of Chenzhou, Lun was transferred to Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Lingkun rose to prominence, Emperor Shizong of Zhou promoted Lun to army aide of Chenzhou; when Lingkun was assigned to govern Chenzhou, Lun was transferred to Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 罷職，復居宛丘，多以不法干郡政，私酤求市利，掊斂民財，公私患之。

translations.literal: When he left office he returned to dwell in Wanqiu, and often interfered in prefectural government by unlawful means, privately distilled liquor to seek market profit, and extorted the people's wealth; both public and private circles were troubled by him.
translations.idiomatic: After leaving office he settled again in Wanqiu, where he repeatedly meddled in prefectural affairs by illegal means, ran a private distillery for profit, and squeezed wealth from the populace until officials and commoners alike were aggrieved.

sentences.zh: 項城民武郁詣闕訴其事，命殿中侍御史率汀按之。

translations.literal: A man of Xiangcheng named Wu Yu went to the capital to lodge complaint about these matters; the court ordered Palace Attendant Censor Shuai Ting to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: A resident of Xiangcheng named Wu Yu traveled to the capital to report these abuses, and the throne ordered Palace Attendant Censor Shuai Ting to conduct an inquiry.

sentences.zh: 倫詐報汀云被詔赴闕，汀奏之。

translations.literal: Lun falsely reported to Ting that he had been summoned by edict to the capital, and Ting memorialized this.
translations.idiomatic: Lun deceived Ting by claiming he had been summoned to court by imperial edict, and Ting reported this to the throne.

sentences.zh: 世宗怒，追劾具狀，法當棄市。

translations.literal: The Emperor Shizong was angry; the case was pursued to a full statement of facts, and by law he should be executed in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong was enraged; investigators pursued the case to a complete finding of fact, and the statute called for public execution.

sentences.zh: 令坤泣請於世宗，遂免死流海島。

translations.literal: Lingkun wept and pleaded with the Emperor Shizong, and he was then spared death and exiled to an island in the sea.
translations.idiomatic: Lingkun wept and begged the emperor for mercy, who then spared Lun's life and banished him to a distant island.

sentences.zh: 顯德六年，為左驍衛中郎將，遷左監門衛將軍。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Xiande he became middle guard of the Left Valiant Cavalry Guards, and was transferred to general of the Left Gate Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Xiande (959) he was made middle guard of the Left Valiant Cavalry Guards, then transferred to general of the Left Gate Guard.

sentences.zh: 宋初，拜磁州刺史，轉亳州團練使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song he was appointed prefect of Cizhou, then transferred to military commissioner of Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of the Song he was appointed prefect of Cizhou, then promoted to regimental commissioner of Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 乾德四年，改本州防禦使，卒。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Qiande he was changed to defense commissioner of his home prefecture, and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Qiande (966) he was made defense commissioner of his native prefecture, where he died.

sentences.zh: 世宗命宰相李穀將兵征淮南，俾令坤等十二將以從。

translations.literal: The Emperor Shizong ordered the chief minister Li Gu to lead troops on campaign against Huainan, and had Lingkun and eleven other generals follow him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong ordered Chief Minister Li Gu to take command of an expedition against Huainan, with Lingkun and eleven other generals placed under him.

sentences.zh: 穀退保正陽，為吳人所乘。

translations.literal: Gu withdrew to defend Zhengyang and was taken advantage of by the Wu forces.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gu fell back to hold Zhengyang, where Wu troops pressed their advantage against him.

sentences.zh: 令坤與宣祖、李重進合兵擊之，大敗吳人。

translations.literal: Lingkun joined forces with Xuanzu and Li Chongjin to strike them and inflicted a great defeat on the Wu army.
translations.idiomatic: Lingkun united with Zhao Kuangyin and Li Chongjin to attack them and routed the Wu forces decisively.

sentences.zh: 世宗親征，聞揚州無備，遣令坤及宣祖、白延遇、趙晁等襲之。

translations.literal: The Emperor Shizong personally campaigned; hearing that Yangzhou was undefended, he dispatched Lingkun together with Xuanzu, Bai Yanyu, Zhao Chao, and others to raid it.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor took the field in person and learned that Yangzhou lay unguarded, he sent Lingkun, Zhao Kuangyin, Bai Yanyu, Zhao Chao, and others to seize it by surprise.

sentences.zh: 令坤先令延遇以精騎數百遲明馳入，城中不之覺。

translations.literal: Lingkun first ordered Yanyu to gallop in at daybreak with several hundred picked horsemen; the city did not detect them.
translations.idiomatic: Lingkun first sent Yanyu ahead with several hundred elite cavalry to charge into the city at dawn before anyone inside knew they were coming.

sentences.zh: 令坤繼至撫之，民皆按堵。

translations.literal: Lingkun arrived afterward to reassure the people, and all the populace remained settled in their homes.
translations.idiomatic: Lingkun followed to pacify the population, and the people remained calm and undisturbed in their homes.

sentences.zh: 南唐東都副留守馮延魯為僧匿寺中，令坤求獲之，送行在，遂以令坤知州事。

translations.literal: Feng Yanlu, Eastern Capital deputy military governor of Southern Tang, hid himself as a monk in a temple; Lingkun sought him out and captured him, sent him to the imperial camp, and then had Lingkun act as prefect in charge of the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Yanlu, the Southern Tang deputy military governor of the eastern capital, had disguised himself as a monk in a temple; Lingkun tracked him down and sent him to the emperor's camp, after which Lingkun was put in charge of the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 由是泰州懼以城降。

translations.literal: Because of this Taizhou, in fear, surrendered its city.
translations.idiomatic: Taizhou, shaken by this turn of events, then surrendered.

sentences.zh: 時錢俶受詔攻常、潤，圍毗陵，反為南唐所敗。

translations.literal: At that time Qian Chu, having received orders to attack Chang and Run, besieged Piling but in turn was defeated by Southern Tang.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Qian Chu of Wuyue, acting on imperial orders to attack Chang and Run prefectures, besieged Piling but was in turn defeated by Southern Tang.

sentences.zh: 南唐乘勝遣將陸孟俊逼泰州，周師不能守，孟俊遂進軍蜀岡，逼揚州，令坤棄其城。

translations.literal: Southern Tang, riding its victory, sent the general Lu Mengjun to press Taizhou; the Zhou army could not hold it. Mengjun then advanced his army to Shugang, pressed Yangzhou, and Lingkun abandoned the city.
translations.idiomatic: Southern Tang pressed its advantage by sending Lu Mengjun against Taizhou; the Zhou garrison could not hold, and Mengjun marched on to Shugang, threatening Yangzhou until Lingkun was forced to abandon the city.

sentences.zh: 世宗怒，命太祖與張永德領兵趨六合援之。

translations.literal: The Emperor Shizong was angry and ordered the future Taizu and Zhang Yongde to lead troops in haste to Liuhe to relieve him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong was furious and ordered Zhao Kuangyin and Zhang Yongde to hurry troops to Liuhe to relieve him.

sentences.zh: 令坤聞援至，復入城守，與孟俊兵戰，大敗之，擒孟俊，敗其將馬貴於楚州灣頭堰，擒漣州刺史秦進崇。

translations.literal: When Lingkun heard that relief had arrived, he re-entered the city to defend it, fought Mengjun's army, and inflicted a great defeat; he captured Mengjun, defeated his general Ma Gui at Wantou weir in Chuzhou, and captured Qin Jinchong, prefect of Lianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that reinforcements had arrived, Lingkun re-entered the city to hold it, engaged Mengjun's army, and won a crushing victory; he took Mengjun prisoner, routed Mengjun's general Ma Gui at the Wantou weir in Chuzhou, and captured Qin Jinchong, prefect of Lianzhou.

sentences.zh: 俄命向拱為緣江招討使，以令坤副之，下壽州。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward Xiang Gong was appointed riverine pacification commissioner, with Lingkun as his deputy, and they advanced on Shouzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Xiang Gong was made riverine pacification commissioner with Lingkun as his deputy, and they marched on Shouzhou.

sentences.zh: 歸朝，加檢校太尉、領鎮安軍節度使。

translations.literal: On returning to court he was given the additional title of Grand Preceptor by inspection and made military governor of Zhen'an Army.
translations.idiomatic: After returning to court he was promoted to honorary Grand Preceptor and appointed military governor of the Zhen'an Army.

sentences.zh: 世宗乃復幸淮右，次楚州，遣令坤率兵先入揚州，命權知軍府事。

translations.literal: The Emperor Shizong then again visited the Huai region in person, halted at Chuzhou, and dispatched Lingkun to lead troops to enter Yangzhou first, ordering him to act provisionally as military prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong then returned in person to the Huai region, stopping at Chuzhou; he sent Lingkun ahead with troops into Yangzhou and appointed him acting military prefect.

sentences.zh: 揚州城為吳人所毀，詔發丁壯別築新城，命令坤為修城都部署。

translations.literal: The city of Yangzhou had been destroyed by the Wu people; an edict ordered able-bodied men levied to build a separate new city, and Lingkun was appointed overall director of the wall construction.
translations.idiomatic: Because Wu forces had wrecked the old city of Yangzhou, the court ordered labor levies to erect a new town elsewhere and named Lingkun overall director of the construction.

sentences.zh: 宋初，移領天平軍，加侍衛馬步軍都指揮使、同平章事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song he was transferred to command Tianping Army, and given the additional posts of commander-in-chief of the palace horse and foot guards and Associate Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of the Song he was transferred to command the Tianping Army and was also made commander-in-chief of the palace horse and foot guards with the rank of Associate Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 太祖親征李筠，詔令坤率兵屯河陽。

translations.literal: When the Taizu personally campaigned against Li Yun, an edict ordered Lingkun to lead troops and encamp at Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizu took the field in person against Li Yun, he ordered Lingkun to lead troops and encamp at Heyang.

sentences.zh: 及澤、潞平，還京，錫宴令坤等於禮賢講武殿，賜襲衣、器幣、鞍勒馬有差，以功加兼侍中。

translations.literal: When Ze and Lu were pacified he returned to the capital; a feast was granted to Lingkun and others in the Hall for Honoring the Worthy and Reviewing Arms, and court robes, ritual vessels, saddles, bridles, and horses were bestowed in differing measure; for his merit he was given the additional post of Vice Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: After Ze and Lu prefectures were pacified he returned to the capital, where the emperor feasted Lingkun and his fellows in the Hall for Honoring the Worthy and Reviewing Arms, bestowing court robes, ritual gifts, saddles, bridles, and horses in varying measure, and promoting him to Vice Grand Councillor for his achievements.

sentences.zh: 又從討李重進。

translations.literal: He again followed on the campaign to suppress Li Chongjin.
translations.idiomatic: He also took part in the campaign against Li Chongjin.

sentences.zh: 建隆二年，改成德軍節度，充北面緣邊兵馬都部署。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianlong he was made military governor of the Chengde Army and appointed overall commander of frontier horse and foot forces on the northern border.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jianlong (961) he was made military governor of the Chengde Army and overall commander of frontier forces on the northern border.

sentences.zh: 將赴鎮，上於別殿置酒餞之，因勖其為治。

translations.literal: As he was about to depart for his command, the emperor set out wine in a side hall to send him off and exhorted him on how to govern.
translations.idiomatic: Before he departed for his post, the emperor entertained him with wine in a side hall and urged him on the principles of good governance.

sentences.zh: 乾德六年，疽發背，卒，年四十六。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Qiande a carbuncle broke out on his back and he died, aged forty-six.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Qiande (968) a carbuncle on his back proved fatal; he was forty-six.

sentences.zh: 太祖素服發哀於講武殿，錄其子慶朝為閑廄使，慶雄為閑廄副使。

translations.literal: The Taizu, in plain dress, proclaimed mourning in the Hall for Reviewing Arms; he enrolled his son Qingchao as commissioner of the imperial stables and Qingxiong as deputy commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizu appeared in plain mourning dress at the Hall for Reviewing Arms to lament him, appointing his son Qingchao commissioner of the imperial stables and Qingxiong deputy commissioner.

sentences.zh: 令坤有才略，識治道，與太祖同事周室，情好親密。

translations.literal: Lingkun had talent and stratagem, understood the way of governance, and had served the Zhou house together with the Taizu; their affection was intimate.
translations.idiomatic: Lingkun possessed ability and strategic insight, understood the principles of governance, and had served the Later Zhou together with Taizu; the two were on terms of close friendship.

sentences.zh: 鎮常山凡七年，北邊以寧。

translations.literal: He governed Changshan for seven years in all, and the northern frontier was thereby tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: He held Changshan for seven years in all, and the northern frontier remained secure throughout.

sentences.zh: 聞其卒，甚悼惜之。

translations.literal: On hearing of his death he deeply mourned and regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: When he heard of Lingkun's death, the emperor grieved deeply.

sentences.zh: 初，南唐遣邊鎬破湖南，以馬希崇分司揚州，及令坤克取之，希崇以妓楊氏獻，令坤甚嬖之。

translations.literal: Earlier Southern Tang had sent Bian Hao to conquer Hunan and placed Ma Xichong in nominal charge at Yangzhou; when Lingkun captured it, Xichong presented the courtesan Lady Yang, and Lingkun doted on her greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Southern Tang had sent Bian Hao to conquer Hunan, Ma Xichong had been left nominally in charge at Yangzhou; after Lingkun took the city, Xichong presented the courtesan Lady Yang to him, and Lingkun became deeply infatuated with her.

sentences.zh: 會擒陸孟俊，將械送行在所，楊氏於簾間窺見之，即拊膺慟哭。

translations.literal: When Lu Mengjun was captured and was about to be sent in fetters to the imperial camp, Lady Yang glimpsed him from behind a curtain and at once beat her breast and wept bitterly.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Mengjun was captured and was to be sent in chains to the imperial camp, Lady Yang caught sight of him from behind a curtain and immediately clutched her breast and burst into bitter weeping.

sentences.zh: 令坤怪，問之，楊氏曰：「孟俊往年入潭州，殺我家二百口，惟妾為希崇所匿得免，願甘心焉。

translations.literal: Lingkun was puzzled and questioned her. Lady Yang said: "In former years Mengjun entered Tanzhou and killed two hundred members of my family; only I, your humble servant, was hidden away by Xichong and thus escaped. I wish to be satisfied in my heart.
translations.idiomatic: Lingkun was astonished and asked her why. Lady Yang said, "Years ago Mengjun entered Tanzhou and slaughtered two hundred members of my family; only I was hidden away by Xichong and thus survived. I have long wished to see him pay with his life.

sentences.zh: 」令坤以詰孟俊，孟俊具狀，令坤乃殺之。

translations.literal: " Lingkun questioned Mengjun on this; Mengjun gave a full account of the facts, and Lingkun then killed him.
translations.idiomatic: " Lingkun confronted Mengjun with her accusation; Mengjun confessed the facts in full, and Lingkun then had him executed.

sentences.zh: 慕容延釗

translations.literal: Murong Yanzhao
translations.idiomatic: Murong Yanzhao

sentences.zh: 慕容延釗，太原人。

translations.literal: Murong Yanzhao was a man of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Yanzhao was a native of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 父章，襄州馬步軍都校、領開州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Zhang was chief commander of horse and foot forces in Xiangzhou and concurrently held the post of prefect of Kaizhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhang had been chief commander of horse and foot forces in Xiangzhou and concurrently prefect of Kaizhou.

sentences.zh: 延釗少以勇幹聞。

translations.literal: Yanzhao in youth was known for courage and competence.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhao was known from youth for his courage and executive ability.

sentences.zh: 漢祖之興也，周祖為其佐命，以延釗隸帳下。

translations.literal: When the Han founder rose, the Zhou founder was his supporter in founding the state, and Yanzhao was placed under his command staff.
translations.idiomatic: When the Later Han founder rose to power, Guo Wei of Later Zhou served as his chief supporter, and Yanzhao was assigned to Wei's personal staff.

sentences.zh: 周廣順初，補西頭供奉官，歷尚食副使、鐵騎都虞候。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhou Guangshun he was appointed attendant of the western bureau, and passed through the posts of deputy commissioner of the imperial pantry and colonel of the Iron Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Guangshun era (951) he was made an attendant of the western bureau, later serving as deputy commissioner of the imperial pantry and colonel of the Iron Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 太祖即位，延釗方握重兵屯真定，帝遣使諭旨，許以便宜從事。

translations.literal: When the Taizu took the throne, Yanzhao was holding heavy forces encamped at Zhending; the emperor sent envoys to convey his intent and permitted him to act as circumstances required.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu ascended the throne, Yanzhao was commanding substantial forces encamped at Zhending; the emperor sent envoys to convey his wishes and authorized him to act at his own discretion.

sentences.zh: 延釗與韓令坤率所部兵按治邊境，以鎮靜聞。

translations.literal: Yanzhao together with Han Lingkun led the troops under their command to pacify the border regions, and were known for keeping the frontier calm.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhao and Han Lingkun led their troops to pacify the frontier, earning renown for keeping the borderlands quiet.

sentences.zh: 太祖嘉之，加殿前都點檢、同中書門下三品，避其父名故也。

translations.literal: The Taizu commended them and gave Yanzhao the additional posts of commander-in-chief of the palace guards and third-rank associate of the Secretariat-Chancellery, because of taboo on his father's name.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu praised their service and promoted Yanzhao to commander-in-chief of the palace guards with third-rank Secretariat status, using this title to avoid the taboo on his father's given name.

sentences.zh: 李筠叛，初命與王全斌由東路會兵進討，俄為行營都部署、知潞州行府事；

translations.literal: When Li Yun rebelled, he was first ordered together with Wang Quanbin to unite forces by the eastern route and advance in suppression; shortly afterward he became overall commander of the campaign encampment and acting military prefect of Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Yun rebelled, Yanzhao was first ordered to join Wang Quanbin on the eastern route for the punitive campaign; he was soon made overall commander of the field headquarters with acting authority over the Luzhou military prefecture.

sentences.zh: 及平，加兼侍中，詔還澶州。

translations.literal: When it was pacified he was given the additional post of Vice Grand Councillor, and by edict returned to Chanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebellion was crushed he was made Vice Grand Councillor as well and ordered back to Chanzhou.

sentences.zh: 建隆二年，長春節來朝，賜宅一區。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianlong he came to court on the Long Spring festival and was granted one residence.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jianlong (961) he came to court for the Long Spring festival and received a residence as a gift.

sentences.zh: 表解軍職，徙為山南東道節度、西南面兵馬都部署。

translations.literal: He memorialized to resign his military post and was transferred to military governor of Shannan East Circuit and overall commander of horse and foot forces on the southwest frontier.
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned to relinquish his military commission and was transferred to military governor of Shannan East Circuit and overall commander of frontier forces in the southwest.

sentences.zh: 是冬大寒，遣中使賜貂裘、百子氈帳。

translations.literal: That winter was bitterly cold; palace envoys were sent to bestow sable fur coats and felt tents with the hundred-children pattern.
translations.idiomatic: That winter was exceptionally severe, and the court sent palace envoys with gifts of sable coats and felt tents patterned with the hundred-children motif.

sentences.zh: 四年春，命師南征，以延釗為湖南道行營前軍都部署。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fourth year troops were ordered south on campaign, and Yanzhao was made overall commander of the vanguard of the Hunan circuit campaign headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the fourth year (963) the court launched a southern campaign and appointed Yanzhao overall commander of the vanguard of the Hunan expeditionary headquarters.

sentences.zh: 時延釗被病，詔令肩輿即戎事。

translations.literal: At that time Yanzhao was afflicted with illness; an edict ordered him to take up military affairs even if carried in a litter.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhao was ill at the time, but the emperor ordered him to take the field even if he had to be carried in a litter.

sentences.zh: 賊將汪端與眾數千擾朗州，延釗擒之，磔於市。

translations.literal: The rebel general Wang Duan with several thousand followers harassed Langzhou; Yanzhao captured him and dismembered him in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel leader Wang Duan was raiding Langzhou with several thousand men; Yanzhao captured him and had him torn apart in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 荊、湘既平，加檢校太尉。

translations.literal: When Jing and Xiang were pacified he was given the additional title of Grand Preceptor by inspection.
translations.idiomatic: After Jing and Xiang were pacified he was promoted to honorary Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 是冬，卒，年五十一。

translations.literal: That winter he died, aged fifty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died that winter at the age of fifty-one.

sentences.zh: 初，延釗與太祖友善，顯德末，太祖任殿前都點檢，延釗為副，常兄事延釗；

translations.literal: From the first Yanzhao and the Taizu were on friendly terms; at the end of Xiande the Taizu held the post of commander-in-chief of the palace guards and Yanzhao was his deputy, and he always treated Yanzhao as an elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhao and Taizu had been close friends from the outset; toward the end of Xiande, when Taizu was commander-in-chief of the palace guards with Yanzhao as his deputy, Taizu always treated Yanzhao as an elder brother.

sentences.zh: 及即位，每遣使勞問，猶以兄呼之。

translations.literal: After he took the throne he frequently sent envoys to inquire after his welfare and still addressed him as elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: After Taizu took the throne he still sent envoys to inquire after him and continued to address him as elder brother.

sentences.zh: 洎寢疾，御封藥以賜，聞其卒，慟哭久之。

translations.literal: When he fell gravely ill, the emperor personally sealed medicine and bestowed it; on hearing of his death he wept bitterly for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: When Yanzhao fell gravely ill, the emperor sent medicine sealed with the imperial signet; on hearing of his death Taizu wept at length.

sentences.zh: 贈中書令，追封河南郡王，錄其子弟授官者四人。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given the title of Secretariat Director, enfeoffed as Prince of Henan Commandery, and four of his sons and younger brothers were enrolled and given offices.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Secretariat Director, ennobled as Prince of Henan Commandery, and four of his sons and younger kinsmen were granted official posts.

sentences.zh: 子德業、德豐、德鈞。

translations.literal: His sons were Deye, Defeng, and Dejun.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Deye, Defeng, and Dejun.

sentences.zh: 德業至衛州刺史；

translations.literal: Deye rose to prefect of Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Deye rose to become prefect of Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 德鈞至尚食副使。

translations.literal: Dejun rose to deputy commissioner of the imperial pantry.
translations.idiomatic: Dejun rose to deputy commissioner of the imperial pantry.

sentences.zh: 延釗弟延忠，歷內殿直、供奉西頭官都知，至磁州刺史；

translations.literal: Yanzhao's younger brother Yanzhong passed through the posts of inner palace attendant, director of the western bureau attendants, and rose to prefect of Cizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhao's younger brother Yanzhong served as inner palace attendant and director of the western bureau attendants before becoming prefect of Cizhou.

sentences.zh: 延卿至虎捷軍都指揮使。

translations.literal: Yanqing rose to commander-in-chief of the Tiger Swift Army.
translations.idiomatic: Another brother, Yanqing, rose to commander-in-chief of the Tiger Swift Army.

sentences.zh: 延卿子德琛。

translations.literal: Yanqing's son was Dechen.
translations.idiomatic: Yanqing's son was Dechen.

sentences.zh: 子 德豐

translations.literal: Son: Defeng
translations.idiomatic: Son: Defeng

sentences.zh: 德豐，字日新，幼聰悟，延釗愛之，嘗曰：「興吾門者必此子。

translations.literal: Defeng, style name Rixin, was clever and perceptive in youth; Yanzhao loved him and once said: "The one who will raise up our house must be this boy.
translations.idiomatic: Defeng, whose style name was Rixin, was clever and quick-witted as a boy; Yanzhao doted on him and once said, "This boy will be the one to bring honor to our house.

sentences.zh: 」八歲，補山南東道衙內指揮使。

translations.literal: " At eight years of age he was appointed commander of the inner guard of the Shannan East Circuit headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: " At the age of eight he was appointed commander of the inner guard of the Shannan East Circuit headquarters.

sentences.zh: 延釗卒，授如京使。

translations.literal: When Yanzhao died he was appointed envoy to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: After Yanzhao's death he was appointed envoy to the capital.

sentences.zh: 開寶中，從征太原，領禦砦南面巡檢。

translations.literal: During Kaibao he followed the campaign against Taiyuan and led inspection of the southern face of the imperial encampment.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaibao era (968–976) he took part in the campaign against Taiyuan as inspector of the southern face of the imperial encampment.

sentences.zh: 又為揚州都監。

translations.literal: He also served as overall supervisor of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as overall military supervisor of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 征南唐，為洞子都監。

translations.literal: On the campaign against Southern Tang he was overall supervisor of sappers.
translations.idiomatic: During the campaign against Southern Tang he was placed in charge of the sapper corps.

sentences.zh: 城既下，命為昇州都監，市廛安靜，澤國富饒，使者多裒聚金帛，德豐獨以廉潔聞。

translations.literal: After the city fell he was ordered to be overall supervisor of Shengzhou; the markets were tranquil and the marsh country was rich, and many envoys amassed gold and silks, but Defeng alone was known for integrity.
translations.idiomatic: After the city fell he was made overall supervisor of Shengzhou; though the markets were orderly and the water country rich, and many officials amassed gold and silks, Defeng alone was known for his integrity.

sentences.zh: 俄領蔚州刺史。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he took charge as prefect of Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed prefect of Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 太平興國二年，知慶州兼邠、寧都巡檢。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taiping Xingguo he was made acting prefect of Qingzhou and concurrently frontier inspector of Bin and Ning.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Taiping Xingguo (977) he was made acting prefect of Qingzhou and concurrently frontier inspector of Bin and Ning circuits.

sentences.zh: 嘗破小遇族，奪名馬數十匹，詔書褒諭。

translations.literal: He once defeated the Xiaoyu tribe and seized several tens of famous horses; an edict praised and commended him.
translations.idiomatic: He once defeated the Xiaoyu tribe and captured several dozen prized horses, for which the throne issued an edict of commendation.

sentences.zh: 居任九年，以簡靜為治，邊鎮安之。

translations.literal: He held office for nine years, governing with simplicity and calm, and the border garrison was thereby secure.
translations.idiomatic: He held the post for nine years, governing with simplicity and restraint, and the frontier remained tranquil throughout.

sentences.zh: 雍熙四年，使登、萊閱強壯，及還，拜西上閣門使。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yongxi he was sent to Deng and Lai to review able-bodied men; on his return he was appointed envoy of the western upper gate.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Yongxi (987) he was sent to Deng and Lai to review able-bodied men for service; on his return he was made envoy of the western upper gate.

sentences.zh: 是冬，出為定遠軍鈐轄，命領後陣中隊，別將萬騎以禦邊害。

translations.literal: That winter he went out as military controller of Dingyuan Army, ordered to lead the rear-array central corps and separately command ten thousand horsemen to guard against border harm.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he was posted as military controller of the Dingyuan Army, charged with commanding the rear-array central corps and an additional ten thousand cavalry to guard against frontier raids.

sentences.zh: 淳化二年，進秩東上，知邢州。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chunhua he was advanced in rank to the eastern upper gate and made acting prefect of Xingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Chunhua (991) he was promoted to envoy of the eastern upper gate and appointed acting prefect of Xingzhou.

sentences.zh: 三年，改判四方館事，出知延州。

translations.literal: In the third year he was changed to administer the Four Directions Hostel and went out as acting prefect of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year (992) he was put in charge of the Four Directions Hostel and sent out to govern Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 時侯延廣知靈武，或言其得西夏情，倔強難制，命德豐代之，就賜白金三千兩。

translations.literal: At that time Hou Yanguang was governing Lingwu; some said he had gained intelligence on the Western Xia and was obstinate and hard to control, so Defeng was ordered to replace him and was thereupon granted three thousand taels of white gold.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Yanguang was then governing Lingwu; some reported that he had inside knowledge of Western Xia affairs yet was obstinate and difficult to control, so Defeng was ordered to replace him and was granted three thousand taels of white gold on the spot.

sentences.zh: 會建使名，改為四方館使。

translations.literal: When the envoy title was established by regulation, he was changed to envoy of the Four Directions Hostel.
translations.idiomatic: When the formal title of hostel envoy was established, his post was retitled envoy of the Four Directions Hostel.

sentences.zh: 未幾，以所部不治，徙知慶州，俄又改靈州兼部署。

translations.literal: Before long, because the troops under his command were not well governed, he was transferred to act as prefect of Qingzhou; shortly afterward he was again changed to Lingzhou with concurrent frontier deployment authority.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, because his command was poorly disciplined, he was transferred to Qingzhou; soon afterward he was reassigned to Lingzhou with concurrent frontier deployment authority.

sentences.zh: 穀價湧貴，德豐出私廩賑饑民，全活者眾。

translations.literal: Grain prices surged; Defeng opened his private granary to relieve the starving people, and many were wholly preserved alive.
translations.idiomatic: When grain prices soared, Defeng opened his private granaries to feed the hungry, saving a great many lives.

sentences.zh: 轉引進使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to reception commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made reception commissioner.

sentences.zh: 賊入境，德豐率兵擊走，獲羊馬甚眾。

translations.literal: When bandits entered the border, Defeng led troops to strike and drive them off, capturing very many sheep and horses.
translations.idiomatic: When raiders crossed the border, Defeng led troops to repulse them and seized a large number of sheep and horses.

sentences.zh: 咸平二年，遷客省使，知鎮州，召對便坐，撫慰甚至。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianping he was moved to commissioner of the guest bureau, made acting prefect of Zhenzhou, summoned to audience at the informal seat, and comforted with exceptional warmth.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xianping (999) he was promoted to commissioner of the guest bureau and made acting prefect of Zhenzhou; summoned to an informal audience, he received exceptional personal reassurance from the throne.

sentences.zh: 是冬，遼人南侵，德豐繕兵固守，餉饋不絕，詔獎之。

translations.literal: That winter the Liao people invaded south; Defeng repaired his troops and held firm, and provisions were supplied without interruption; an edict commended him.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, when the Khitan invaded from the north, Defeng drilled his troops and held the line while keeping supplies flowing without interruption, for which the court issued a commendation.

sentences.zh: 三年，改滄州。

translations.literal: In the third year he was transferred to Cangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year (1000) he was transferred to Cangzhou.

sentences.zh: 德豐輕財好施，厚享將士。

translations.literal: Defeng held wealth lightly and delighted in giving; he richly entertained officers and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Defeng was generous with his wealth and treated his officers and soldiers lavishly.

sentences.zh: 在西邊時，母留京師，妻孥寓長安，貧甚，真宗憫之，特詔給團練使奉。

translations.literal: While he was on the western frontier his mother remained in the capital and his wife and children lodged in Chang'an in great poverty; Emperor Zhenzong pitied them and specially ordered that they be given the stipend of a regimental commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: While he served on the western frontier his mother remained in the capital and his wife and children lived in Chang'an in dire poverty; Emperor Zhenzong took pity on them and specially ordered that they receive a regimental commissioner's stipend.

sentences.zh: 逾年，進潁州團練使，知貝、瀛二州。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was advanced to regimental commissioner of Yingzhou and made acting prefect of Bei and Ying prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was promoted to regimental commissioner of Yingzhou with concurrent authority over Bei and Ying prefectures.

sentences.zh: 五年，卒，年五十五。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he died, aged fifty-five.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he died at the age of fifty-five.

sentences.zh: 家無餘財，談者善之。

translations.literal: His household had no surplus wealth, and those who spoke of him praised this.
translations.idiomatic: He left no surplus wealth in his household, and commentators praised him for it.

sentences.zh: 子惟素，至殿內承制。

translations.literal: His son Weisu rose to drafter within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: His son Weisu rose to become a palace drafter.

sentences.zh: 從子 德琛

translations.literal: Nephew: Dechen
translations.idiomatic: Nephew: Dechen

sentences.zh: 德琛以延釗蔭補供奉官，累遷內殿崇班、知夔州。

translations.literal: Dechen, through Yanzhao's privilege, was appointed attendant and was repeatedly promoted to honored officer of the inner palace and acting prefect of Kuizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Through Yanzhao's hereditary privilege Dechen entered service as an attendant and rose to honored officer of the inner palace and acting prefect of Kuizhou.

sentences.zh: 李順之亂，賊酋張餘領眾十萬餘、舟千艘來寇，與順戰龍山，斬首千餘級；

translations.literal: During the rebellion of Li Shun, the bandit chieftain Zhang Yu led more than a hundred thousand followers and a thousand boats to raid; he fought Shun at Longshan and beheaded more than a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: During Li Shun's rebellion the bandit leader Zhang Yu led more than a hundred thousand men and a thousand boats against the government; Dechen fought Shun at Longshan and took more than a thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 又與白繼贇擊賊，斬二萬餘，悉焚其舟。

translations.literal: He again joined Bai Jiyun in striking the bandits, beheaded more than twenty thousand, and burned all their boats.
translations.idiomatic: He then joined Bai Jiyun in attacking the rebels, killing more than twenty thousand and burning all their vessels.

sentences.zh: 賊剽開州，圍雲安，德琛往援之，又斬百餘級。

translations.literal: When bandits plundered Kaizhou and besieged Yun'an, Dechen went to relieve them and again beheaded more than a hundred.
translations.idiomatic: When rebels raided Kaizhou and besieged Yun'an, Dechen marched to their relief and took another hundred-odd heads.

sentences.zh: 累詔褒諭。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly commended by imperial edict.
translations.idiomatic: The throne repeatedly issued edicts praising his service.

sentences.zh: 歷西京作坊、左藏二副使。

translations.literal: He passed through the posts of deputy commissioner of the western capital workshops and of the left treasury.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as deputy commissioner of the western capital workshops and of the left treasury.

sentences.zh: 咸平二年，轉崇儀副使、荊湖北路鈐轄。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianping he was transferred to deputy commissioner of honored ritual and military controller of Jinghu North Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xianping he was made deputy commissioner of honored ritual and military controller of Jinghu North Circuit.

sentences.zh: 蠻擾澧、鼎境上，德琛戰於北氵義，奪耕牛、鎧甲，斬馘以歸。

translations.literal: When barbarians harassed the borders of Li and Ding, Dechen fought at Beiyi, seized plow oxen and armor, and returned with severed heads.
translations.idiomatic: When tribal forces raided the borders of Li and Ding prefectures, Dechen fought them at Beiyi, capturing plow oxen and armor and returning with enemy heads.

sentences.zh: 徙峽路鈐轄，未至，復知夔州。

translations.literal: He was moved to military controller of the Gorges route; before he arrived he was again made acting prefect of Kuizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to military controller of the Gorges route, but before he could take up the post he was again appointed acting prefect of Kuizhou.

sentences.zh: 景德中，領梧州刺史，復任峽路，再遷莊宅使，又為並、代鈐轄，知憲州。

translations.literal: During Jingde he took charge as prefect of Wuzhou, again held the Gorges route, was twice promoted to commissioner of crown estates, then became military controller of Bing and Dai and acting prefect of Xianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jingde era he governed Wuzhou, returned to the Gorges command, was twice promoted to commissioner of crown estates, and later served as military controller of Bing and Dai circuits with acting authority over Xianzhou.

sentences.zh: 天禧初，改右監門衛大將軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianxi he was changed to great general of the Right Gate Guard.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Tianxi era he was made great general of the Right Gate Guard.

sentences.zh: 符彥卿

translations.literal: Fu Yanqing
translations.idiomatic: Fu Yanqing

sentences.zh: 符彥卿，字冠侯，陳州宛丘人。

translations.literal: Fu Yanqing, style name Guanhou, was a man of Wanqiu in Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Yanqing, whose style name was Guanhou, was a native of Wanqiu in Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 父存審，後唐宣武軍節度、蕃漢馬步軍都總管兼中書令。

translations.literal: His father Cunshen was military governor of the Xuanwu Army under Later Tang and overall commander of barbarian and Han horse and foot forces, concurrently Secretariat Director.
translations.idiomatic: His father Cunshen had been military governor of the Later Tang Xuanwu Army, overall commander of barbarian and Han forces, and concurrently Secretariat Director.

sentences.zh: 彥卿年十三，能騎射。

translations.literal: Yanqing at thirteen could ride and shoot.
translations.idiomatic: Yanqing could ride and shoot by the age of thirteen.

sentences.zh: 事莊宗於太原，以謹愿稱，出入臥內，及長，以為親從指揮使。

translations.literal: He served Emperor Zhuangzong at Taiyuan and was known for cautious sincerity, entering and leaving the sleeping quarters; when he grew up he was made commander of the personal guard.
translations.idiomatic: He served Emperor Zhuangzong at Taiyuan, where his cautious and dutiful character won trust enough to admit him to the imperial sleeping quarters; when he came of age he was made commander of the personal guard.

sentences.zh: 入汴，遷散員指揮使。

translations.literal: On entering Bian he was transferred to commander of the loose guard.
translations.idiomatic: After the court moved to Bian he was promoted to commander of the loose guard.

sentences.zh: 郭從謙之亂，莊宗左右皆引去，惟彥卿力戰，射殺十數人，俄矢集乘輿，遂慟哭而去。

translations.literal: During the rebellion of Guo Congqian, Zhuangzong's attendants all withdrew, but Yanqing alone fought fiercely, shooting down more than ten men; shortly arrows clustered on the imperial carriage, and he then wept bitterly and departed.
translations.idiomatic: During Guo Congqian's mutiny all of Zhuangzong's attendants fled, but Yanqing alone fought on, killing more than ten assailants with his bow; when arrows soon riddled the imperial carriage he wept and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 天成三年，以龍武都虞候、吉州刺史討王都於定州，大破契丹於嘉山。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tiancheng, as colonel of the Dragon Martial Guards and prefect of Jizhou, he campaigned against Wang Du at Dingzhou and inflicted a great defeat on the Khitan at Jiashan.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tiancheng, as colonel of the Dragon Martial Guards and prefect of Jizhou, he campaigned against Wang Du at Dingzhou and routed the Khitan at Jiashan.

sentences.zh: 明年克其城，授耀州團練使。

translations.literal: The next year he captured the city and was appointed regimental commissioner of Yaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he took the city and was appointed regimental commissioner of Yaozhou.

sentences.zh: 改慶州刺史。

translations.literal: He was changed to prefect of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made prefect of Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 奉詔築堡方渠北烏侖山口，以招党項。

translations.literal: By imperial order he built a fort north of Fangqu at Wulunshan Pass to attract the Tangut.
translations.idiomatic: On imperial orders he built a fort north of Fangqu at Wulun Pass to win over the Tangut tribes.

sentences.zh: 清泰初，改易州，兼領北面騎軍，賜戎服、介胄、戰馬。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qingtai he was transferred to Yizhou and concurrently commanded northern cavalry; he was granted military dress, armor, and war horses.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Qingtai he was transferred to Yizhou with concurrent command of northern cavalry and was granted military dress, armor, and war horses.

sentences.zh: 嘗射獵遂城鹽臺淀，一日射麞、彘、狼、狐、兔四十二，觀者神之。

translations.literal: He once hunted at Yantai Marsh in Suicheng and in one day shot forty-two deer, boar, wolves, foxes, and hares; onlookers regarded him as divine.
translations.idiomatic: Once while hunting at Yantai Marsh near Suicheng he brought down forty-two deer, boar, wolves, foxes, and hares in a single day, astonishing all who watched.

sentences.zh: 晉天福初，授同州節度。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Later Jin Tianfu he was appointed military governor of Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Later Jin Tianfu era he was made military governor of Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 兄彥饒亦鎮滑臺。

translations.literal: His elder brother Yanrao also governed Huatai.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Yanrao also held Huatai as his command.

sentences.zh: 俄而彥饒叛，彥卿上表待罪，乞田里，晉祖釋不問。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward Yanrao rebelled; Yanqing submitted a memorial awaiting punishment and begged for retirement to the countryside; the Jin founder released him without inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: When Yanrao soon afterward rebelled, Yanqing submitted a memorial accepting blame and begging to retire to the countryside; the Jin founder pardoned him without further inquiry.

sentences.zh: 改左羽林統軍，俄兼領右羽林，改鎮鄜延。

translations.literal: He was changed to commander of the Left Feathered Forest Guards, shortly afterward also commanded the Right Feathered Forest, and was transferred to govern Yan-Yan Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was made commander of the Left Feathered Forest Guards, soon took the Right Feathered Forest as well, and was transferred to govern Yan-Yan Circuit.

sentences.zh: 少帝幼與彥卿狎，即位，召還，出鎮河陽三城。

translations.literal: The young emperor had been intimate with Yanqing in youth; on taking the throne he summoned him back and sent him out to govern the three cities of Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: The young emperor had been close to Yanqing since childhood; on his accession he recalled him and then posted him to govern the three cities of Heyang.

sentences.zh: 遼人南侵，詔彥卿率所部拒戰澶州。

translations.literal: When the Liao people invaded south, an edict ordered Yanqing to lead his troops to resist them in battle at Chanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan invaded from the north, he was ordered to lead his troops against them at Chanzhou.

sentences.zh: 契丹騎兵數萬圍高行周於鐵邱，諸將莫敢當其鋒，彥卿獨引數百騎擊之，遼人遁去，行周得免。

translations.literal: Several tens of thousands of Khitan horsemen besieged Gao Xingzhou at Tieqiu; none of the generals dared meet their edge, but Yanqing alone led several hundred horsemen to strike them; the Liao people fled, and Xingzhou was saved.
translations.idiomatic: Tens of thousands of Khitan cavalry had Gao Xingzhou surrounded at Tieqiu, and none of the other generals dared meet their charge; Yanqing alone led several hundred horsemen into the attack, driving the Khitan off and saving Xingzhou.

sentences.zh: 又副李守貞討平青州楊光遠，移鎮許州，封祁國公。

translations.literal: He again served as deputy to Li Shouzhen in suppressing Yang Guangyuan of Qingzhou, was transferred to govern Xuzhou, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: He next served under Li Shouzhen in suppressing Yang Guangyuan of Qingzhou, was transferred to Xuzhou, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Qi.

sentences.zh: 開運二年，與杜重威、李守貞經略北鄙。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaiyun he joined Du Chongwei and Li Shouzhen in securing the northern frontier.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Kaiyun he joined Du Chongwei and Li Shouzhen in operations along the northern frontier.

sentences.zh: 契丹主率眾十餘萬圍晉師於陽城，軍中乏水，鑿井輒壞，爭絞泥吮之，人馬多渴死，時晉師居下風，將戰，弓弩莫施。

translations.literal: The Khitan ruler led more than a hundred thousand men to surround the Jin army at Yangcheng; the army lacked water, and every well they dug collapsed; they struggled over mud to suck it, and many men and horses died of thirst; at that time the Jin army was downwind, and when about to fight their bows and crossbows could not be deployed.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan ruler led more than a hundred thousand men to surround the Jin army at Yangcheng; water ran so short that every well they dug collapsed and soldiers fought over mud to suck moisture, until men and horses died of thirst in great numbers; the Jin force was downwind, and when battle was joined their bows could not reach the enemy.

sentences.zh: 彥卿謂張彥澤、皇甫遇曰：「與其束手就擒，曷若死戰，然未必死。

translations.literal: Yanqing said to Zhang Yanze and Huangfu Yu: "Rather than wait with bound hands to be captured, how much better to fight to the death — yet one may not necessarily die.
translations.idiomatic: Yanqing told Zhang Yanze and Huangfu Yu, "Better to fight to the death than surrender with bound hands — and we may not die at all.

sentences.zh: 」彥澤等然之。

translations.literal: " Yanze and the others agreed.
translations.idiomatic: " Yanze and the others agreed.

sentences.zh: 遂潛兵尾其後，順風擊之，契丹大敗，其主乘橐駝以遁，獲其器甲、旗仗數萬以歸。

translations.literal: They then secretly sent troops to follow behind them and, with the wind at their backs, struck; the Khitan suffered a great defeat, their ruler fled riding a camel, and they returned with tens of thousands of weapons, armor, banners, and implements.
translations.idiomatic: They sent troops quietly to follow the Khitan rear and struck with the wind at their backs; the Khitan were routed, their ruler fled on a camel, and the Jin army returned with tens of thousands of captured weapons, armor, banners, and gear.

sentences.zh: 少帝嘉之，改武寧軍節度、同平章事。

translations.literal: The young emperor commended him and made him military governor of the Wuning Army and Associate Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: The young emperor praised him and appointed him military governor of the Wuning Army with the rank of Associate Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 為左右所間，會再出師河朔，彥卿不預，易其行伍，配以羸師數千，戍荊州口。

translations.literal: Slandered by those around the throne, when troops were again sent north of the Yellow River Yanqing was not included; his unit was changed and he was assigned several thousand weak troops to garrison Jingzhoukou.
translations.idiomatic: Slandered at court, he was passed over when the army marched again into Hebei; his command was reorganized and he was left with several thousand weak troops to garrison Jingzhoukou.

sentences.zh: 及杜重威以大軍降於滹水，急詔彥卿與高行周領禁兵屯澶淵。

translations.literal: When Du Chongwei surrendered the great army at the Hutuo River, an urgent edict ordered Yanqing and Gao Xingzhou to lead palace troops to encamp at Chanyuan.
translations.idiomatic: When Du Chongwei surrendered the main army at the Hutuo River, urgent orders went out for Yanqing and Gao Xingzhou to lead palace troops to Chanyuan.

sentences.zh: 會彥澤引遼兵入汴，彥卿與行周遂歸遼。

translations.literal: When Yanze led Liao troops into Bian, Yanqing and Xingzhou then submitted to the Liao.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Yanze led Khitan troops into Bian, Yanqing and Xingzhou submitted to the Liao.

sentences.zh: 遼主以陽城之敗詰彥卿，彥卿對曰：「臣事晉王，不敢愛死，今日之事，死生唯命。

translations.literal: The Liao ruler questioned Yanqing over the defeat at Yangcheng; Yanqing replied: "I served the Prince of Jin and did not spare my life; as for today's affair, life and death are only as fate decrees.
translations.idiomatic: The Liao ruler questioned him about the defeat at Yangcheng; Yanqing replied, "I served the Prince of Jin and never shrank from death; as for today, my life is entirely in your hands.

sentences.zh: 」遼主笑而釋之。

translations.literal: " The Liao ruler laughed and released him.
translations.idiomatic: " The Liao ruler laughed and let him go.

sentences.zh: 會徐、宋寇盜蠭起，遼主即遣歸鎮。

translations.literal: When bandits swarmed up in Xu and Song, the Liao ruler at once sent him back to his command.
translations.idiomatic: When banditry flared in Xu and Song, the Liao ruler promptly sent him back to his post.

sentences.zh: 行次甬橋，賊魁李仁恕擁眾數萬攻徐州。

translations.literal: Passing Yongqiao, the bandit chief Li Renshu gathered several tens of thousands to attack Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At Yongqiao the bandit leader Li Renshu mustered tens of thousands of men to attack Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 彥卿領數十騎遽至城下，仁恕遣其徒執彥卿馬，請隨入城，俄頃，彥卿子昭序自城中遣軍校陳守習縋而出，大呼賊中曰：「相公當為國討賊，何故自入虎口，乃助賊攻城？

translations.literal: Yanqing led several tens of horsemen in haste to the foot of the wall; Renshu sent his followers to seize Yanqing's horse and asked him to enter the city with them; shortly Yanqing's son Zhaoxu from within the city sent the military officer Chen Shouxi down by rope, who shouted among the bandits: "The chief minister ought to fight bandits for the state — why enter the tiger's maw yourself and help bandits attack the city?
translations.idiomatic: Yanqing galloped to the walls with only a few dozen horsemen; Renshu's men seized his horse and urged him to enter the city with them; soon his son Zhaoxu sent the officer Chen Shouxi down on a rope from the battlements, who shouted to the rebels, "My father should be destroying bandits for the state — why throw himself into the tiger's maw and help rebels storm his own city?

sentences.zh: 我雖父子，今為讎敵，當死戰，城不可入！

translations.literal: Though we are father and son, we are now foe and foe; I shall fight to the death — the city must not be entered!
translations.idiomatic: Father and son though we are, we are enemies now; I will fight you to the death — you shall not enter this city!

sentences.zh: 」賊惶愧，羅拜彥卿前，乞免罪，彥卿為設誓，乃解去。

translations.literal: " The bandits were alarmed and ashamed, ranged themselves in obeisance before Yanqing, and begged to be spared; Yanqing set an oath for them, and they then dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: " The rebels, shamed and afraid, kowtowed before Yanqing and begged forgiveness; he bound them with an oath, and they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 漢祖入汴，彥卿自徐州來朝，改鎮兗州，加兼侍中。

translations.literal: When the Han founder entered Bian, Yanqing came from Xuzhou to court, was transferred to govern Yanzhou, and given the additional post of Vice Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: When the Later Han founder entered Bian, Yanqing came from Xuzhou to court, was transferred to Yanzhou, and was made Vice Grand Councillor as well.

sentences.zh: 乾祐中，加兼中書令，封魏國公，拜守太保，移鎮青州。

translations.literal: During Qianyou he was given the additional post of Secretariat Director, enfeoffed as Duke of Wei, appointed Defender Grand Preceptor, and transferred to govern Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During Qianyou he was made Secretariat Director as well, enfeoffed as Duke of Wei, appointed Defender Grand Preceptor, and transferred to Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 及殺楊邠輩，召促赴闕下。

translations.literal: When Yang Bin and his faction were killed, he was urgently summoned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: After Yang Bin and his associates were executed, he was urgently summoned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 世宗初，幷人擾潞州，潞兵敗，命彥卿領兵從磁州固鎮路壓其背。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shizong's reign the Bingzhou people harassed Luzhou; the Luzhou army was defeated, and Yanqing was ordered to lead troops by the Guzhen road from Cizhou to press their rear.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Shizong's reign the forces of Bingzhou raided Luzhou and defeated its garrison; Yanqing was ordered to advance by the Guzhen road from Cizhou and strike their rear.

sentences.zh: 及帝親征，命為行營一行都部署兼知太原行府事，領步騎二萬進討。

translations.literal: When the emperor campaigned in person, he was appointed overall commander of the first campaign encampment and acting military prefect of the Taiyuan field headquarters, leading twenty thousand foot and horse to advance in suppression.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor took the field in person, Yanqing was made overall commander of the first field headquarters with acting authority over the Taiyuan military prefecture, leading twenty thousand infantry and cavalry against the enemy.

sentences.zh: 初，彥卿之行也，世宗以幷人雖敗，朝廷饋運不繼，未議攻擊，且令觀兵城下，徐圖進取。

translations.literal: At first, when Yanqing set out, Shizong thought that though the Bingzhou people had been defeated, the court's supply transport was not continuous and no attack was yet discussed; he was only ordered to observe the army below the walls and slowly plan advance and seizure.
translations.idiomatic: When Yanqing first marched out, Shizong judged that although the Bingzhou forces had been beaten, court supply lines were still unreliable and ordered no immediate assault; Yanqing was told to observe the enemy below the walls and plan a gradual advance.

sentences.zh: 及周師入境，汾、晉吏民望風款接，皆以久罹虐政，願輸軍須以資兵力，世宗從之。

translations.literal: When the Zhou army entered the territory, officials and people of Fen and Jin received them with submission at sight of the wind; all, having long suffered harsh government, wished to supply military needs to support the army's strength, and Shizong assented.
translations.idiomatic: Once Zhou troops crossed the border, officials and commoners throughout Fen and Jin submitted at the first approach; after years of harsh rule they offered supplies to sustain the army, and Shizong accepted.

sentences.zh: 而連下數州，彥卿等皆以芻糧未備，欲旋軍。

translations.literal: But having taken several prefectures in succession, Yanqing and the others all said that fodder and grain were not ready and wished to withdraw the army.
translations.idiomatic: After several prefectures fell in succession, Yanqing and the other commanders argued that fodder was not yet ready and urged a withdrawal.

sentences.zh: 世宗不之省，乃調山東近郡輓軍食濟之。

translations.literal: Shizong did not heed this and instead mobilized nearby commanderies east of the mountains to transport army grain to supply them.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong would not hear of it and instead requisitioned grain from nearby commanderies east of the mountains to feed the army.

sentences.zh: 及世宗至城下，命與郭從義、向訓、白重贊、史彥超率萬騎屯忻口，以拒北援，又下盂縣。

translations.literal: When Shizong reached the foot of the walls, he ordered Yanqing together with Guo Congyi, Xiang Xun, Bai Chongzan, and Shi Yanchao to lead ten thousand horsemen to encamp at Xinkou to block northern relief, and also took Mengxian.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong arrived below the walls he ordered Yanqing, Guo Congyi, Xiang Xun, Bai Chongzan, and Shi Yanchao to hold Xinkou with ten thousand cavalry against northern reinforcements, and Mengxian was also taken.

sentences.zh: 遼人駐忻北，遊騎及近郊，史彥超以二千騎當其鋒，左右馳擊，彥超死之；

translations.literal: The Liao people encamped north of Xin; their scouting horsemen reached the near suburbs; Shi Yanchao with two thousand horsemen met their edge and charged left and right; Yanchao died in the fight.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan encamped north of Xin and their scouts reached the suburbs; Shi Yanchao met their vanguard with two thousand horsemen and charged to either flank, but was killed in the fighting.

sentences.zh: 敗遼眾二千餘，遼騎遁走。

translations.literal: They defeated more than two thousand Liao troops, and the Liao horsemen fled.
translations.idiomatic: They routed more than two thousand Khitan troops and drove their cavalry off.

sentences.zh: 先鋒為遼人所掩，重傷數百人，諸將論議矛盾，師故不振。

translations.literal: The vanguard was ambushed by the Liao people; several hundred were gravely wounded; the generals' counsels conflicted, and the army therefore did not rally.
translations.idiomatic: The vanguard was ambushed by the Khitan, several hundred men were badly wounded, and the generals could not agree on a course of action, so the army failed to regain momentum.

sentences.zh: 世宗乃班師，數賜彥卿繒綵、鞍勒馬，遣歸本鎮。

translations.literal: Shizong then withdrew the army, repeatedly bestowed on Yanqing silks and saddled horses, and sent him back to his original command.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong then withdrew the army, repeatedly rewarded Yanqing with silks and saddled horses, and sent him back to his original post.

sentences.zh: 還京，拜彥卿太傅，改封魏王。

translations.literal: On returning to the capital he appointed Yanqing Grand Preceptor and changed his enfeoffment to Prince of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Back in the capital he was made Grand Preceptor and ennobled as Prince of Wei.

sentences.zh: 恭帝即位，加守太尉。

translations.literal: When the Gong emperor took the throne, he was given the additional title of Defender Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gong succeeded, he was made Defender Grand Marshal as well.

sentences.zh: 太祖即位，加守太師。

translations.literal: When the Taizu took the throne, he was given the additional title of Defender Grand Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu took the throne, he was made Defender Grand Mentor.

sentences.zh: 建隆四年春，來朝，賜襲衣、玉帶。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fourth year of Jianlong he came to court and was granted court robes and a jade belt.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the fourth year of Jianlong he came to court and received court robes and a jade belt.

sentences.zh: 宴射於金鳳園，太祖七發皆中的，彥卿貢名馬稱賀。

translations.literal: At an archery feast in the Golden Phoenix Garden the Taizu with seven shots all hit the mark; Yanqing presented a famous horse in congratulation.
translations.idiomatic: At an archery feast in the Golden Phoenix Garden Taizu hit the mark with all seven shots, and Yanqing presented a famed horse in congratulation.

sentences.zh: 開寶二年六月，移鳳翔節度，被病肩輿赴鎮，至西京，上言疾亟，請就醫洛陽，從之。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the second year of Kaibao he was transferred to military governor of Fengxiang; afflicted with illness he went to his command in a litter; reaching the western capital he reported that his illness was severe and begged to seek medical treatment in Luoyang, and this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the second year of Kaibao he was transferred to Fengxiang; ill, he traveled to his post in a litter; at the western capital he reported that his illness was grave and begged to seek treatment in Luoyang, which was granted.

sentences.zh: 假滿百日，猶請其奉，為御史所劾，下留司御史臺。

translations.literal: When his leave of a hundred days was full he still requested his stipend; he was impeached by the censors and sent down to the retained censorate.
translations.idiomatic: When his hundred-day leave expired he still claimed his stipend; censors impeached him and the case went to the retained censorate.

sentences.zh: 太祖以姻舊特免推鞫，止罷其節制。

translations.literal: The Taizu, because of marriage ties and old friendship, specially exempted him from interrogation and only removed his military governorship.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu, owing to their kinship by marriage and long friendship, specially spared him interrogation and merely stripped him of his military command.

sentences.zh: 八年六月，卒，年七十八。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the eighth year he died, aged seventy-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the sixth month of the eighth year at the age of seventy-eight.

sentences.zh: 喪事官給。

translations.literal: Funeral expenses were supplied by the government.
translations.idiomatic: Official funds covered his funeral.

sentences.zh: 彥卿將家子，勇略有謀，善用兵。

translations.literal: Yanqing was a general's son, brave and resourceful with stratagem, skilled in employing troops.
translations.idiomatic: Yanqing was born into a military family, brave and resourceful, and skilled in the use of troops.

sentences.zh: 存審之第四子，軍中謂之『符第四』。

translations.literal: He was Cunshen's fourth son; in the army he was called "Fu the Fourth."
translations.idiomatic: As Cunshen's fourth son, the army knew him as "Fu the Fourth."

sentences.zh: 前後賞賜鉅萬，悉分給帳下，故士卒樂為效死。

translations.literal: Rewards before and after totaled tens of thousands, all distributed to those under his command, so the soldiers were glad to die in his service.
translations.idiomatic: Rewards to him over the years ran to vast sums, all of which he distributed among the men under his command, so his soldiers were glad to fight to the death for him.

sentences.zh: 遼人自陽城之敗，尤畏彥卿，或馬病不飲齕，必唾而咒曰：「此中豈有符王邪？

translations.literal: Since the defeat at Yangcheng the Liao people especially feared Yanqing; if a horse was ill and would not eat or bite fodder, they would spit and curse: "Can Prince Fu be in this place?
translations.idiomatic: After the defeat at Yangcheng the Khitan especially feared Yanqing; if a horse fell sick and refused fodder, they would spit and curse, "Surely Prince Fu cannot be here?

sentences.zh: 」晉少主既陷契丹，德光之母問左右曰：「彥卿安在？

translations.literal: " After the young Jin emperor had fallen into Khitan hands, Deguang's mother asked those around her: "Where is Yanqing?
translations.idiomatic: " After the young Jin emperor had fallen into Khitan hands, Empress Dowager Yelü, mother of Emperor Taizong, asked her attendants, "Where is Yanqing?

sentences.zh: 」或對曰：「聞其已遣歸徐州矣。

translations.literal: " Someone answered: "It is heard that he has already been sent back to Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: " Someone answered, "I hear he has already been sent back to Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 」德光母曰：「留此人中原，何失策之甚！

translations.literal: " Deguang's mother said: "To leave this man in the Central Plains — how extreme a lapse of strategy!
translations.idiomatic: " The empress dowager said, "To leave such a man in the Central Plains — what a blunder!

sentences.zh: 」其威名如此。

translations.literal: " His renown was such.
translations.idiomatic: " Such was the terror of his name.

sentences.zh: 鎮大名餘十年，政委牙校劉思遇。

translations.literal: He governed Daming for more than ten years and entrusted administration to his military adjutant Liu Siyu.
translations.idiomatic: He held Daming for more than ten years and left daily administration to his adjutant Liu Siyu.

sentences.zh: 思遇貪黠，怙勢斂貨財，公府之利多入其家，彥卿不之覺。

translations.literal: Siyu was greedy and cunning, relied on power to gather goods and wealth, and most of the public office's profits entered his household; Yanqing did not perceive it.
translations.idiomatic: Siyu was greedy and cunning, used his power to amass wealth, and diverted most of the commandery's profits into his own household while Yanqing remained unaware.

sentences.zh: 時藩鎮率遣親吏受民租，概量增溢，公取其餘羨，而魏郡尤甚。

translations.literal: At that time military governors commonly sent trusted clerks to collect the people's rent, broadly measuring with surplus, and the public office took the remaining excess; Wei Commandery was especially severe.
translations.idiomatic: Military governors commonly sent trusted agents to collect rents, measuring grain generously and keeping the surplus for themselves, and Wei Commandery was among the worst offenders.

sentences.zh: 太祖聞之，遣常參官主其事，由是斛量始平。

translations.literal: The Taizu heard of this and sent a regular attendee to take charge of the matter; from this the bushel measure at last became fair.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu learned of this he sent a regular court official to take charge, and grain measures at last became fair.

sentences.zh: 詔以羨餘粟賜彥卿，以愧其心。

translations.literal: An edict bestowed the surplus grain on Yanqing to shame his heart.
translations.idiomatic: An edict granted Yanqing the surplus grain as a rebuke meant to stir his conscience.

sentences.zh: 彥卿酷好鷹犬，吏卒有過，求名鷹犬以獻，雖盛怒必貰之。

translations.literal: Yanqing was ardently fond of hawks and hounds; if clerks and soldiers committed faults, they sought famed hawks and hounds to present, and even in great anger he would pardon them.
translations.idiomatic: Yanqing was passionately fond of falcons and hunting dogs; subordinates who erred could win pardon even from his fiercest rage by presenting prized birds or hounds.

sentences.zh: 性不飲酒，頗謙恭下士，對賓客終日談笑，不及世務，不伐戰功。

translations.literal: By nature he did not drink wine, was rather modest and deferential to scholars, with guests laughed and talked all day without touching on worldly affairs, and did not boast of battle merit.
translations.idiomatic: He did not drink, treated scholars with modest courtesy, spent whole days laughing and talking with guests without touching on public affairs, and never boasted of his battlefield achievements.

sentences.zh: 居洛陽七八年，每春月，乘小駟從家僮一二遊僧寺名園，優遊自適。

translations.literal: Dwelling in Luoyang seven or eight years, each spring month he rode a small team with one or two household servants to visit monks' temples and famous gardens, roaming at ease to please himself.
translations.idiomatic: During the seven or eight years he lived in Luoyang, each spring he would take a light carriage with one or two servants to wander among monasteries and famous gardens at his leisure.

sentences.zh: 周世宗宣懿皇后、太宗懿德皇后，皆彥卿女也。

translations.literal: Zhou Shizong's Empress Xuanyi and Taizong's Empress Yide were both daughters of Yanqing.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Xuanyi of Emperor Shizong of Zhou and Empress Yide of Emperor Taizong of Song were both Yanqing's daughters.

sentences.zh: 自恭帝及太祖兩朝，賜詔書不名。

translations.literal: From the Gong emperor through the Taizu across two reigns, edicts granted to him omitted his personal name.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout the reigns of Emperor Gong and Taizu, edicts addressed to him omitted his personal name.

sentences.zh: 子昭信、昭愿、昭壽。

translations.literal: His sons were Zhaoxin, Zhaoyuan, and Zhaoshou.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Zhaoxin, Zhaoyuan, and Zhaoshou.

sentences.zh: 昭信，天雄軍衙內都指揮使、領賀州刺史。

translations.literal: Zhaoxin was commander of the inner guard of the Tianxiong Army headquarters and concurrently prefect of Hezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaoxin was commander of the inner guard of the Tianxiong Army headquarters and concurrently prefect of Hezhou.

sentences.zh: 周顯德初，卒，贈檢校太保、閬州防禦使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhou Xiande he died and was posthumously given the titles of Grand Guardian by inspection and defense commissioner of Langzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He died early in the Xiande era and was posthumously made honorary Grand Guardian and defense commissioner of Langzhou.

sentences.zh: 子 昭愿

translations.literal: Son: Zhaoyuan
translations.idiomatic: Son: Zhaoyuan

sentences.zh: 昭愿，字致恭，謹厚謙約，頗讀書好士。

translations.literal: Zhaoyuan, style name Zhigong, was cautious, generous, modest, and restrained, read books considerably, and loved scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaoyuan, whose style name was Zhigong, was cautious, sincere, and modest, devoted himself to study, and delighted in the company of scholars.

sentences.zh: 周廣順中，以蔭補天雄軍牙職，俄領興州刺史。

translations.literal: During Zhou Guangshun, through privilege he was appointed to a staff post in the Tianxiong Army, and shortly took charge as prefect of Xingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the Guangshun era he entered service through hereditary privilege as a staff officer of the Tianxiong Army and soon became prefect of Xingzhou.

sentences.zh: 開寶中，改領恩州。

translations.literal: During Kaibao he was changed to take charge of Enzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaibao era he was transferred to govern Enzhou.

sentences.zh: 彥卿養疾居洛，入補供奉官。

translations.literal: While Yanqing was convalescing in Luoyang, he entered the capital to be appointed attendant.
translations.idiomatic: While Yanqing convalesced in Luoyang, Zhaoyuan went to the capital and was appointed a palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 四年，改領羅州刺史。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was changed to take charge as prefect of Luozhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was transferred to govern Luozhou.

sentences.zh: 七年，遷西京作坊副使。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was moved to deputy commissioner of the western capital workshops.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was made deputy commissioner of the western capital workshops.

sentences.zh: 俄授尚食使，出護陳、許、蔡、潁等州巡兵。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was appointed commissioner of the imperial pantry and went out to guard the patrol troops of Chen, Xu, Cai, Ying, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made commissioner of the imperial pantry and sent out to oversee patrol troops in Chen, Xu, Cai, Ying, and neighboring prefectures.

sentences.zh: 從征太原，為御營四面巡檢使。

translations.literal: He followed the campaign against Taiyuan as inspector of all four faces of the imperial encampment.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in the campaign against Taiyuan as inspector of the imperial encampment on all four sides.

sentences.zh: 及攻幽州，命與定國軍節度偓率兵萬餘，置砦城南。

translations.literal: When they attacked Youzhou, he was ordered together with Wo, military governor of the Dingguo Army, to lead more than ten thousand troops and set up a stockade south of the city.
translations.idiomatic: During the assault on Youzhou he was ordered to join Wo, military governor of the Dingguo Army, in leading more than ten thousand men to build a stockade south of the city.

sentences.zh: 師還，真拜蔡州刺史，知幷澶二州。

translations.literal: When the army returned he was formally appointed prefect of Caizhou and given acting authority over Bing and Chan prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: After the army withdrew he was formally appointed prefect of Caizhou with concurrent authority over Bing and Chan prefectures.

sentences.zh: 不逾月，復移幷門兼副部署。

translations.literal: Within less than a month he was again transferred to Bing Gate with the additional post of deputy deployment commander.
translations.idiomatic: Within a month he was reassigned to Bing Gate with the additional post of deputy deployment commander.

sentences.zh: 丁內艱，起復，為本州團練使，連知永興軍、梓滑二州。

translations.literal: When his mother died he left mourning and was recalled, made regimental commissioner of his home prefecture, and in succession acted as prefect of Yongxing Army and of Zi and Hua prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: After his mother's death he was recalled from mourning to serve as regimental commissioner of his home prefecture and in succession governed Yongxing Army and Zi and Hua prefectures.

sentences.zh: 咸平初，又為天雄軍、邢州二鈐轄。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianping he again became military controller of the Tianxiong Army and Xingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Xianping era he again served as military controller of the Tianxiong Army and Xingzhou.

sentences.zh: 三年，以疾求歸京師，詔遣中使、尚醫馳傳診視。

translations.literal: In the third year, because of illness he begged to return to the capital; an edict sent palace envoys and the imperial physician by express relay to examine him.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he petitioned to return to the capital on account of illness, and the throne sent palace envoys and the imperial physician by express relay to examine him.

sentences.zh: 既還，帝賜以名方御藥，拜本州防禦使。

translations.literal: After he returned, the emperor bestowed famous prescription imperial medicines and appointed him defense commissioner of his home prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Once he had returned, the emperor granted him renowned imperial prescriptions and made him defense commissioner of his home prefecture.

sentences.zh: 四年，卒，年五十七。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he died, aged fifty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourth year at the age of fifty-seven.

sentences.zh: 車駕臨哭，贈鎮東軍節度。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage came in person to mourn; he was posthumously given the post of military governor of the Zhendong Army.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor came in person to mourn him and posthumously made him military governor of the Zhendong Army.

sentences.zh: 子承煦，為左千牛衛將軍。

translations.literal: His son Chengxu was general of the Left Thousand-Ox Guard.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chengxu became general of the Left Thousand-Ox Guard.

sentences.zh: 子 昭壽

translations.literal: Son: Zhaoshou
translations.idiomatic: Son: Zhaoshou

sentences.zh: 昭壽，初補供奉官。

translations.literal: Zhaoshou was first appointed attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaoshou first entered service as a palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 開寶七年，改西京作坊副使。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Kaibao he was changed to deputy commissioner of the western capital workshops.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Kaibao he was made deputy commissioner of the western capital workshops.

sentences.zh: 歷遷六宅副使、領蘭州刺史。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to deputy commissioner of the Six Residences and took charge as prefect of Lanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the posts of deputy commissioner of the Six Residences and prefect of Lanzhou.

sentences.zh: 雍熙二年冬，命與劉知信護鎮州屯兵。

translations.literal: In the winter of the second year of Yongxi he was ordered together with Liu Zhixin to guard the encamped troops at Zhenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the second year of Yongxi he was ordered to guard the encamped troops at Zhenzhou together with Liu Zhixin.

sentences.zh: 命遣將北征，又與知信為押隊都監，轉尚食使，真拜光州刺史。

translations.literal: When generals were dispatched on the northern expedition, he again served with Zhixin as overall escort supervisor, was transferred to commissioner of the imperial pantry, and was formally appointed prefect of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the court sent generals on the northern expedition, he again served with Zhixin as overall escort supervisor, was made commissioner of the imperial pantry, and was formally appointed prefect of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 端拱二年，知洪州。

translations.literal: In the second year of Duangong he was made acting prefect of Hongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Duangong he was made acting prefect of Hongzhou.

sentences.zh: 淳化四年，改定州。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Chunhua he was transferred to Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Chunhua he was transferred to Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 咸平初，遷鳳州團練使、益州鈐轄。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianping he was moved to regimental commissioner of Fengzhou and military controller of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Xianping era he was made regimental commissioner of Fengzhou and military controller of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 昭壽以貴家子日事遊宴，簡倨自恣，常紗帽素氅衣，偃息後圃，不理戎務，有所裁決，即令家人傳道。

translations.literal: Zhaoshou, as a son of an eminent house, daily devoted himself to feasting and pleasure, was curt and arrogant and indulged himself, often wore gauze cap and plain cloak, reclined to rest in the rear garden, did not attend to military affairs, and whenever there was a decision ordered a family member to convey it.
translations.idiomatic: As a scion of a great house Zhaoshou spent his days in feasting and diversion, aloof and self-indulgent; he commonly wore a gauze cap and plain cloak, lounged in his rear garden, neglected military affairs, and had family members relay whatever decisions he made.

sentences.zh: 多集錦工就廨舍織纖麗綺帛，每有所須，取給於市，餘半歲方給其直，又令部曲私邀取之。

translations.literal: He gathered many brocade artisans at his official quarters to weave fine and gorgeous silks; whenever he needed something he took supplies from the market and only after half a year paid the price, and also had his retainers privately intercept goods.
translations.idiomatic: He gathered brocade weavers at his official residence to produce fine silks; whenever he needed goods he took them from the market and paid only after half a year, and also had his retainers seize supplies on the side.

sentences.zh: 廣糴黍稻，未及成熟者亦取之，悉貯寺觀中，久之損敗，即勒道釋償之。

translations.literal: He broadly purchased millet and rice, and even took grain not yet ripe; he stored it all in temples and monasteries, and when after long time it spoiled he compelled Daoists and Buddhists to compensate for it.
translations.idiomatic: He bought up grain in large quantities, taking even crops before they ripened, and stored it all in temples and monasteries; when it eventually spoiled he forced monks and priests to pay compensation.

sentences.zh: 縱其下淩忽軍校。

translations.literal: He allowed his subordinates to insult and disregard military officers.
translations.idiomatic: He allowed his subordinates to bully and disrespect army officers.

sentences.zh: 劍南自李順平後，人心洶洶，知州牛冕緩馳無政，昭壽又不能御軍，人皆怨憤。

translations.literal: In Jiannan, since Li Shun was pacified, popular sentiment was turbulent; the acting prefect Niu Mian was lax and slow and had no government, Zhaoshou also could not control the army, and all were resentful and angry.
translations.idiomatic: After Li Shun's rebellion was crushed in the Sword South region popular unrest remained high; Acting Prefect Niu Mian was lax and ineffective, Zhaoshou could not control his troops, and resentment spread everywhere.

sentences.zh: 神衛卒趙延順等八人謀，欲害昭壽，未敢發。
